findings.title: New `dashboard.mobileOverview` query has zero tests despite complex branching business logic
findings.why_it_matters: mobileOverview is the single backend query powering the entire mobile dashboard (openDealsCount, overdueActivitiesCount, overdueInvoicesTotal, revenueMTD, recentActivities, overdueInvoices). Its handler contains many behavioral branches that a silent regression would break the whole mobile home screen with no safety net: (1) the UNAUTHORIZED `if (!orgId)` throw, (2) openDealsCount filter excludes won/lost/archived, (3) overdueActivitiesCount requires dueAt + not-completed + not-cancelled + dueAt<now, (4) recentActivities sorts ascending by dueAt and slices top 5, (5) overdueInvoices filters posted + !archived + dueDate<now and slices top 5, (6) revenueMTD filters type==='customer_invoice' && state!=='cancel' && !archived and sums totalAmount. None of these conditions is exercised by any test in this diff. The only dashboard test (dashboardStructure.test.ts) asserts static local literals for the OLD `overview` query and does not touch mobileOverview at all.
findings.evidence: `git diff` shows mobileOverview added (convex/dashboard.ts:273). `find` shows no test referencing mobileOverview. convex/__tests__/dashboardStructure.test.ts only mirrors the `overview` return shape with hardcoded local constants and does not import or call the real query.
findings.suggested_fix: Add convex/__tests__/mobileOverview.test.ts (or extend dashboardStructure.test.ts) covering: missing org → UNAUTHORIZED throw; a deal mix where some are won/lost/archived and asserting only open deals are counted; an activity set with mixed status (planned/done/cancelled) and dueAt undefined, asserting only overdue open ones are counted; invoices with mixed state/type/archived, asserting overdue total + revenue MTD are correct; and the top-5 slice + due-date ordering.

findings.title: New `dashboard.agingDeals` query and the in-`overview` aging computation are untested
findings.why_it_matters: agingDeals is a newly exported query with substantive branching logic: it computes avgDaysPerStage from won deals (default 14, recomputed only when wonDeals.length>=3 via a reduce with a 30-day fallback and 365-day cap, then divided by 3 with a Math.max(...,7) floor), classifies each active deal as isAging when daysInStage>avgDaysPerStage, filters to aging only, and sorts descending. The same logic is duplicated inside `overview`. A bug here (e.g. the `totalDays / wonDeals.length / 3` divisor, or the `stageEnteredAt ?? _creationTime` fallback) would silently mislabel stale deals as healthy. No test verifies the baseline=14 path, the >=3 won-deals recompute path, the isAging threshold, or the sort direction.
findings.evidence: convex/dashboard.ts:196 (agingDeals) and convex/dashboard.ts:138-176 (in-overview aging) are new. No test file references agingDeals or asserts the computed avgDaysPerStage / isAging classification.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests asserting: (a) with 0-2 won deals, avgDaysPerStage stays 14 and a deal 15 days in stage is aging while one 13 days in stage is not; (b) with 3+ won deals the recomputed threshold is used; (c) result is filtered to isAging only and sorted by daysInStage desc; (d) missing org throws UNAUTHORIZED.

findings.title: AuthProvider provider-level behavior is entirely untested; only the pure reducer is covered
findings.why_it_matters: auth-machine.test.ts thoroughly covers the pure authStateReducer, but the provider that drives navigation has critical untested behavior: (1) toAuthSession() validates session/user shape and returns null on malformed data — a bug here would crash the app on a bad Better Auth payload or silently fail auto-login; (2) the useSession effect dispatches TOKEN_REVOKED + scrubs secure storage on error and SESSION_RESOLVED otherwise — the error branch is the security-critical 'poisoned cookie' scrub path; (3) signInEmail normalizes both result.error.message and thrown errors into a user-facing string; (4) signOut runs clearSecureAuthStorage() + convexClient.clearAuth() in a finally block even when the server signOut throws, which is the 'never strand local state' guarantee. The reducer tests give false confidence that auth is covered when the actual integration glue is not.
findings.evidence: auth-machine.test.ts imports only authStateReducer/initialAuthState/isAuthBusy (line 16). No test imports AuthProvider, toAuthSession, signInEmail, or signOut. The diff adds no test for auth-provider.tsx.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a react-test-renderer or @testing-library/react-native test (with authClient mocked) asserting: toAuthSession rejects payloads missing session.id/user.id/email and accepts valid ones; the useSession error effect clears secure storage and dispatches TOKEN_REVOKED; signInEmail surfaces both result.error and thrown errors; signOut clears storage + Convex auth even when authSignOut() rejects.

findings.title: formatMoney / formatCurrency / formatCurrencyCompact pure formatting functions have no tests
findings.why_it_matters: These render every money figure on the mobile app (KPIs, invoice rows, invoice detail totals, overdue totals). They contain real branches: null/NaN → '—'; negative amounts get a '-' sign; IDR path rounds to whole and groups with dots; non-IDR path uses 2 decimals + comma grouping; formatCurrencyCompact switches rb/jt/M suffixes at 1_000/1_000_000/1_000_000_000 and prepends '-' for negatives. A regression in groupThousands (the manual digit grouping loop) or the compact thresholds would silently produce wrong amounts on Hermes where Intl locale support varies. The comments explicitly call out that these must match the web output, so exact-string assertions are the right test.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/format-money.ts:23 (formatMoney), apps/mobile/src/lib/format.ts:10 (formatCurrency) and :27 (formatCurrencyCompact) are new pure functions. No format-money.test.ts / format.test.ts exists in the diff or repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Add lib/format-money.test.ts and lib/format.test.ts with table-driven assertions: formatMoney(null/undefined/NaN)==='—'; formatMoney(1234567,'IDR')==='Rp 1.234.567'; formatMoney(-123)==='Rp -123'; a non-IDR currency yields 2 decimals with comma grouping; formatCurrencyCompact at the three magnitude boundaries and for a negative value.

findings.title: Invoice overdue classifier and StatusBadge branch logic are untested
findings.why_it_matters: isInvoiceOverdue is the classifier driving the overdue filter in invoices/index.tsx, the destructive badge, the day-count in 'Overdue Nd', and the amount/row coloring. The code was clearly written with deterministic testing in mind (it accepts an injected `now`), yet no test exists. Uncovered branches: state must be exactly 'posted'; amountDue must be >0 (a paid-but-posted invoice is not overdue); dueDate must be a number; dueDate must be < now. The StatusBadge switch (paid/draft/cancel/posted/default) and the 'Overdue Nd' day computation are also untested. A regression that, e.g., drops the amountDue>0 guard would reclassify every posted invoice as overdue.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/invoice-row.tsx:41 exports isInvoiceOverdue and :50 StatusBadge, both new. No invoice-row.test.ts exists. The invoices list and detail screens depend on this classifier.
findings.suggested_fix: Add components/invoice-row.test.ts (the pure helpers can be tested without RN): isInvoiceOverdue true only when posted && amountDue>0 && dueDate<number && typeof dueDate==='number'; false for draft/paid/cancel, amountDue===0, or dueDate===undefined; and a quick StatusBadge mapping table.

findings.title: MutationButton status machine (idle→running→success/error, double-press guard) is untested
findings.why_it_matters: MutationButton is the shared mutation-feedback control the plan says every form should use, and it owns non-trivial state: a running press must ignore a second press (isBusy guard); a resolved onPress transitions to 'success' and auto-resets to idle after successDurationMs via a guarded setState that only flips back if still 'success'; a rejected onPress sets an error message preferring errorLabel then the thrown Error.message then a default. None of these transitions or the success-state self-reset timer are verified. This is the kind of component where a subtle bug (e.g. dropping the `current === 'success'` guard) re-enables the button early or strands a stuck spinner.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/mutation-button.tsx:50 handlePress is new. No mutation-button.test.ts in the diff or repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a component test using fake timers: press while running is a no-op; successful onPress → success label shown then back to idle after successDurationMs; rejected onPress → error message from Error.message, or from errorLabel when provided; button disabled while running and success.

findings.title: secure-storage catch branches (locked keystore / deleteItem failure) are untested
findings.why_it_matters: This module is the security boundary for persisted sessions. Every method deliberately swallows exceptions and returns null/no-op so a locked iOS keychain degrades to 'no session' instead of crashing. That graceful-degradation behavior is exactly what must be tested: getItem must return null (not throw) when SecureStore.getItem throws; setItem must not throw when SecureStore.setItem throws; clearSecureAuthStorage must continue deleting remaining keys when one deleteItem throws; readSecureValue must return null on throw. Because expo-secure-store is the only dependency and it is trivially mockable, these are cheap pure tests. An uncaught regression here would either crash the app on a locked device or silently fail to scrub credentials on sign-out (the 'stolen device' security posture the comments emphasize).
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/secure-storage.ts:62 (getItem try/catch), :69 (setItem try/catch), :83 (clearSecureAuthStorage per-key try/catch), :94 (readSecureValue try/catch). No secure-storage.test.ts exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add lib/secure-storage.test.ts mocking expo-secure-store: assert getItem returns null and does not throw when getItem throws; setItem does not throw when setItem throws; clearSecureAuthStorage deletes all keys even when an early deleteItem throws; SECURE_KEYS use the shared prefix so they stay in sync with @crm/config.

findings.title: NetworkProvider connectivity state machine and polling/app-state branches are untested
findings.why_it_matters: network.test.ts covers the pure helpers (probeNetwork, nextNetworkState, shouldMarkOffline) but the provider that wires them into app behavior is untested, and it holds the actual correctness the user sees: the consecutiveFailuresRef threshold gating (only mark offline after OFFLINE_THRESHOLD failures), the 'wasRecentlyOffline' success flash shown only when transitioning offline→online (with timer reset/clear), the .catch() path that increments failures and may flip offline but notably does NOT update lastCheckedAt (an inconsistency vs the .then path), the AppState 'active' foreground re-probe, and the poll interval skipping probes when the app is backgrounded. Because nextNetworkState/shouldMarkOffline are pure, the integration of the failure counter + restored flash is the only place these are exercised and it has no test.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/providers/network-provider.tsx:75 checkNow, :~110 poll effect, :~143 AppState effect are new. network.test.ts only imports from ./network, not the provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a provider test (RN test environment, mock expo-secure-store/AppState/fetch and use fake timers) asserting: two consecutive probe failures are required before isOnline flips false; a single success after offline sets wasRecentlyOffline and later clears it; returning to 'active' triggers a probe; and the catch path increments the failure counter.

findings.title: New-activity form validation and due-time computation have no tests
findings.why_it_matters: The CreateActivitySchema and the DUE_OPTIONS time math are the validation/correctness core of the only write screen in the MVP. Untested branches: title trim + min(1)/max(200); type must be in USER_ACTIVITY_TYPES (status_change excluded); entityType must be in ENTITY_TYPES; the 'tonight' option has a real branching bug-prone path (if the computed 6PM is <= now, roll to tomorrow's 6PM); the default-due fallback when dueKey is unknown; and handleSubmit's safeParse failure → fieldErrors mapping plus the catch that puts the mutation error on the title field. The 'tonight' midnight-rollover branch especially is a classic off-by-one that only a test with a mocked Date.now will catch.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/app/(app)/activities/new.tsx:44 CreateActivitySchema, :~95 DUE_OPTIONS (atHour/tonight rollover), :145 handleSubmit. No activities/new.test.ts exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the schema and DUE_OPTIONS.compute into a testable module (or export them) and add a test: empty/overlong title errors; status_change type rejected; 'tonight' before vs after 6PM (mock Date.now) yields same-day vs next-day 6PM; unknown dueKey falls back to the default; safeParse maps issues onto fieldErrors.

findings.title: formatDistanceToNow / date pattern formatter have no tests
findings.why_it_matters: formatDistanceToNow renders every activity's due label and is documented to handle NaN timestamps by returning '—' (the activity-row edge case). The DIVISIONS loop and the Math.round on the relative diff have boundary behavior worth pinning. The pattern-based format() has a patternToOptions branch tree (MMMM vs MMM vs MM vs M; yyyy/yy; dd/d) that a regression could break (e.g. 'MM/dd/yyyy' or 'yyyy-MM-dd' producing wrong output). These are pure, dependency-light, and run in plain Node, so they are low-cost to cover.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/format-date.ts:29 formatDistanceToNow, :57 format, :84 patternToOptions are new. No format-date.test.ts exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add lib/format-date.test.ts: formatDistanceToNow(NaN)==='—'; a future vs past date yields the right sign and unit; format() on the four documented patterns produces the expected locale-formatted strings; an invalid date returns '—'.

findings.title: ActivityRow overdue detection and type-label fallback are untested
findings.why_it_matters: ActivityRow computes isOverdue from the raw dueAt (NaN-guarded) and selects a Badge variant/label from lookup maps with fallbacks (capitalize for unknown types, 'secondary' variant default). The overdue tone (destructive vs muted) is what makes overdue items 'pop' on the dashboard, and the type maps are the source of truth for badge meaning. An unknown-type regression or a dropped Number.isFinite guard would mislabel rows. The overdue-vs-future and NaN-to-'—' branches are the ones worth pinning.
findings.evidence: apps/mobile/src/components/activity-row.tsx:~54 ActivityRow with typeBadgeVariant/typeLabel fallbacks and the isOverdue Number.isFinite guard. No activity-row.test.ts exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Either export the pure lookup/overdue helpers and test them, or add a lightweight render test asserting the overdue row uses the destructive tone, a future due is muted, and an unknown type falls back to a capitalized label + 'secondary' variant.

findings.title: parseEnv validation/branching in @crm/config has no tests
findings.why_it_matters: parseEnv is the fail-fast gate both web and mobile rely on for a valid CONVEX_URL/SITE_URL/BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, and the mobile config.ts deliberately stubs BETTER_AUTH_SECRET to satisfy it. Untested behavior: the happy path returns defaulted values (CONVEX_SITE_URL and SITE_URL defaults); a missing CONVEX_URL throws a multi-line error listing the field; safeParseEnv returns the Zod result without throwing; NODE_ENV defaults to 'production'. Because mobileEnv() memoizes the first (possibly throwing) call, a regression in error formatting or defaults surfaces as a confusing startup crash with no test to catch it.
findings.evidence: packages/config/src/env.ts:60 parseEnv and :76 safeParseEnv are part of the new @crm/config surface consumed by mobile. No env.test.ts exists in packages/config.
findings.suggested_fix: Add packages/config/src/env.test.ts: valid input with defaults applied; missing CONVEX_URL throws an Error whose message names CONVEX_URL; safeParseEnv returns success/failure objects; NODE_ENV defaults to production when omitted.

findings.title: dashboardStructure.test.ts asserts hardcoded local literals, not the real query output (false confidence)
findings.why_it_matters: This test is presented as guarding the dashboard return contract, but it never imports convex/dashboard.ts. OVERVIEW_SHAPE and the item objects are local constants written by hand in the test file, so the assertions only ever prove the test author's own literals match themselves. If the real query's Zod `returns` schema drops or renames a field, this test still passes. This is worse than no test because it signals coverage that does not exist, and it specifically fails to guard the newly added mobileOverview/agingDeals return shapes. Pre-existing, but it newly misleads on a diff that adds two queries.
findings.evidence: convex/__tests__/dashboardStructure.test.ts defines OVERVIEW_SHAPE inline (line ~13) and asserts against it; there is no import from convex/dashboard.ts and no call to overview/mobileOverview/agingDeals.
findings.suggested_fix: Either import the real query validators and assert against their parsed output shape, or delete this file in favor of integration tests that actually invoke overview/mobileOverview/agingDeals and assert on returned data.

residual_risks: No React Native component/integration test harness is configured for apps/mobile (no test script in package.json, no vitest RN preset visible). Pure-logic extraction is the pragmatic path for most findings, but provider/render behavior (AuthProvider, NetworkProvider, MutationButton) will need @testing-library/react-native or react-test-renderer set up, which this review could not confirm is installed.

convex query handlers are not unit-tested in this repo style (tests like activities.test.ts/deals.test.ts appear to test domain logic, not Convex function execution). mobileOverview/agingDeals findings assume the team can either add a Convex test harness or extract the pure aggregation logic; if neither is feasible, the dashboard query logic remains a residual blind spot.

network.test.ts 'aborts the request after the timeout' asserts ok:false and that a signal was passed, but does not verify the AbortController actually aborts the in-flight fetch or that the timeout timer is cleared on success — minor abort-propagation gap, not elevated to a finding.

E2E/interaction coverage for the auth flow (login → dashboard redirect, sign-out confirmation dialog) is absent; only the pure reducer is covered. A broken navigation pivot (app/index.tsx Redirect logic) would not be caught by any current test.
testing_gaps: Zero tests for any new convex query handler (mobileOverview, agingDeals) — backend behavioral coverage gap.
Zero tests for the mobile provider/integration layer (AuthProvider, NetworkProvider, ConvexClientProvider) — only pure helpers are covered.
Zero tests for mobile pure formatting utilities (format-money, format, format-date, utils/cn).
Zero tests for mobile shared components with branching logic (InvoiceRow classifier, ActivityRow, MutationButton, ErrorBoundary).
Zero tests for the only write screen's form validation and due-time computation (activities/new.tsx).
Zero tests for @crm/config parseEnv and @crm/auth session helpers (toSessionUser, isSessionPayload) added in this branch.
